_doc: What each wired gate catches, and whether anything ELSE catches the same class.
This file exists to make the 2026-08-23 council's retire-candidate rule
evaluable instead of arguable. That rule, report-only: a gate is a retire
CANDIDATE when it has zero live denies in 7 days AND its catch-class is
already owned by pre-commit or ops/ci.sh AND it sits on the hot path.
Two of those three come from measurement — ops/hook-telemetry-rollup.py reads
live denies from out/hook-telemetry.jsonl and derives hot-path membership from
the wiring in ops/config/hooks.json. The third cannot be measured; somebody has
to look at the other control and confirm it covers the same class.
So 'also_caught_by' defaults to "unverified" and MUST stay that way until
someone checks. An unverified entry is never reported as a retire candidate —
a gate deleted on a guess about who else was watching is exactly the incident
this system keeps having. The rollup prints how many entries are still
unverified, so the gap is visible rather than silently empty.
also_caught_by vocabulary:
"unverified"            nobody has checked. The default. Blocks candidacy.
"none-known"            checked, and this gate is the only control. Blocks candidacy.
"pre-commit:<check>"    ops/githooks/pre-commit runs <check>, verified.
"ops-ci:<class>"        ops/ci.sh's <class> covers it, verified.
Add the date and initials of the check in 'verified'.

canonical-edit-gate.py.catch_class: an edit to a file git already tracks inside the shared canonical checkout, at the moment of the edit
canonical-edit-gate.py.verified: 2026-09-01 — checked against the two controls that look like they overlap and do not. ops/githooks/pre-commit refuses a commit on `main` and the PR-only ruleset rejects a direct push, but both bind LATER, at commit/push/merge; by then the dirty state already exists in the shared tree, which is the whole failure this gate catches. No pre-commit check and no ops/ci.sh class sees a file edit before it lands. The class is unowned at this binding moment.
canonical-edit-gate.py.note: REINSTATED 2026-09-01 (Joe's ruling 7f48abf6, Repo Hygiene Program R02) after WR-000019 slice S3 retired it on 2026-08-27. NOTE FOR THE RETIRE-CANDIDATE RULE: this gate shows zero true positives for its first windows simply because it did not exist during them, and ops/gate-lifecycle-report.py already proposes retirement on that basis. 'none-known' blocks candidacy, which is the correct outcome — a quiet window here means the shared tree stayed clean, not that the gate is redundant.

guard-unattended.py.verified: 2026-08-23 — no pre-commit or ops/ci.sh check sees a tool call before it runs; both are commit-time and this is call-time. Nothing else covers it.
guard-unattended.py.note: Fires on every Bash and WebFetch. Highest-volume gate in the stack.

gate-edit-gate.py.catch_class: an ordinary gate edit is announced; a brand-new BLOCKING gate with no admission card is still denied
gate-edit-gate.py.verified: 2026-08-23 — ops/githooks/pre-commit runs staged-gate-bless-check.py, and ops/ci.sh's gates class runs hooks/gate-integrity.py --strict.
gate-edit-gate.py.note: WR-000019 slice S3 (2026-08-27): the ordinary-edit path no longer denies anything to prevent — it announces, and CODEOWNERS + the PR-only ruleset + required CI are what actually keep an enforcement-code edit from reaching main without review. The admission-card sub-case (a NEW blocking gate born with no seven-question card) still denies and is not touched by this change; retiring THAT half would be a separate, considered decision, not an inference from a zero-deny week.

record-home-gate.py.catch_class: record written to a file instead of the database (rule 14181e60)

bash-write-gate.py.catch_class: the Bash door onto record-home-gate and one-repo-gate's policies
bash-write-gate.py.verified: 2026-08-23 — it exists precisely because the file-tool gates did not see Bash; no commit-time check covers a write that never becomes a commit.
bash-write-gate.py.note: Decides nothing itself: it extracts write targets and delegates to the two policy gates.

close-before-open-gate.py.catch_class: new work opened while prior work is unclosed

settings-change-gate.py.note: WR-000019 slice S3 (2026-08-27): the PreToolUse half no longer denies an unreasoned settings change — it announces, and the reason's durable home moved to the PR-description convention CODEOWNERS and required CI now enforce. PostToolUse still records the outcome unconditionally.

draft-export-gate.py.catch_class: draft exported outside the sanctioned path

executor-tier-gate.py.catch_class: subagent dispatched with no named model tier

model-floor-gate.py.catch_class: work below the model floor for its class

escalation-gate.py.catch_class: question escalated to the human that the system should settle

blocker-decider-gate.py.catch_class: blocker recorded with no decider named

rule-shape-gate.py.catch_class: taught rule with no trigger or audit shape

run-record-gate.py.catch_class: drift claim or assertion recorded without a run record

lint-gate.py.catch_class: writing lint on a file just written

map-architecture-gate.py.catch_class: map work finished without the doctrine front door

conduct-stop-gate.py.catch_class: conduct violation in the turn being ended

ledger-sweep.py.catch_class: ruling in the turn that belongs in the decision ledger

context-handoff-gate.py.catch_class: context threshold crossed without a verified same-task successor takeover
context-handoff-gate.py.verified: 2026-08-31 — no other hook preserves precompact high-water and binds Stop to immutable cross-surface takeover evidence.

scheduled-run-record.py.catch_class: scheduled run finishing with no run row

chat-lint-gate.py.catch_class: writing lint on the turn's prose

chat-lint-carryover.py.catch_class: carryover of the previous turn's lint

loose-work-gate.py.catch_class: turn ended with loose work outstanding

drift-assertion-gate.py.catch_class: drift asserted at turn end without a record

gate-integrity.py.catch_class: gate content or wiring drifted from the blessed baseline
gate-integrity.py.verified: 2026-08-23 — ops/ci.sh's gates class runs hooks/gate-integrity.py --strict, the same check.
gate-integrity.py.note: SessionStart, not the hot path, so the retire rule does not reach it.
